summary: FixIt Now should be a modular monolith in BLR1 (Bangalore). Client: Next.js (web) + Expo (Android). Server: NestJS. Data: PostgreSQL (DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL in BLR1 (Bangalore)). Host: DigitalOcean App Platform in BLR1 (Bangalore).

frontend.justification: FixIt Now is a marketplace on web, android. Twelve month target 30,000 users, peak 800, MVP 8 weeks, 3 intermediate engineers. React framework with server rendering and static export, so public pages can rank and logged-in screens can still be rich. One TypeScript codebase for Android and iOS, with expo-sqlite for offline rows. seo_critical is true, so the public URL has to return real HTML. Team languages: javascript, typescript, python.

alternatives.why_not: Nuxt (web) + Expo (Android) is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.
SvelteKit (web) + Expo (Android) is a weaker match for a marketplace with these priorities. Fewer ready-made enterprise component kits than React.

tradeoffs: Heavier than a pure static generator when every page is Markdown.
Framework upgrades need attention each major.
On a 2 GB phone the JS runtime is heavier than Kotlin. Ship a release build and keep screens dull.

backend.justification: A structured TypeScript API. Modules map to orders, chat, and payments without a microservice split. Peak 800, workload balanced, realtime on.

alternatives.why_not: FastAPI is a weaker match for a marketplace with these priorities. You assemble auth, migrations, and admin yourself. Django has those, FastAPI does not.
Fastify is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.

tradeoffs: The decorator style is more framework than Fastify, which is fine at three people and noisy at one.

database.justification: Relational, ACID, and available as a managed service in Mumbai, the EU, and the US. The default for money, bookings, and tenancy. Placement follows the host pin: BLR1 (Bangalore).

alternatives.why_not: MySQL is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.
Microsoft SQL Server is a worse fit for a monthly infra budget of 150 USD.

tradeoffs: A single small node will not meet 99.99 on its own. You pay for a standby.
Very large analytical scans want a column store beside it, not instead of it, once you pass a few terabytes.

hosting.justification: cloud_preference is any, deployment_model is managed_cloud, data_residency resolves to india. The pin is BLR1 (Bangalore). A small PaaS with a Bangalore region (BLR1), managed Postgres, and Spaces. The bill is readable. team.has_devops is false, so a host with a small control surface beats a cluster.

alternatives.why_not: Azure App Service is a worse fit for a monthly infra budget of 150 USD.
Google Cloud Run is a worse fit for a monthly infra budget of 150 USD.

tradeoffs: Past a few thousand concurrent sockets you want a hyperscaler.
Fewer compliance attestations than AWS or Azure.

supporting.justification: Peak concurrency is 800. A small cache holds sessions, OTP attempts, and hot reads so the database is not the first thing to fall over.

alternatives.choice: An in-process cache inside the API
alternatives.why_not: The managed cache is the same protocol with backups and a patch cycle already solved.

tradeoffs: Another process to watch. At a small size it can share a node with the queue.

supporting.justification: Node already speaks this queue, so webhooks get retries without a new vendor. Payments, scoring, or write spikes should retry on their own.

alternatives.why_not: The workload is not on AWS, so SQS would be a second cloud.

tradeoffs: Poison messages need a dead-letter view, or they vanish into retries.

supporting.justification: full_text_search is true and the stored text is about 50.0 GB. A database index answers that without another service to patch.

alternatives.why_not: A dedicated search box is the right upgrade once relevance or the index size hurts, and it is not the MVP constraint.

tradeoffs: Database search is good, not magical. Ranking tweaks are SQL, not a tuning UI.

supporting.justification: Phone OTP for users in India should use a domestic SMS route (DLT-registered). MSG91 is that route. Store only a hash of the code, in the India database.

alternatives.why_not: It works, and it is a worse fit for the residency of the phone numbers.
The user record would sit in a Google project whose region story is easy to get wrong, and phone-auth pricing surprises small budgets.

tradeoffs: SMS cost scales with logins, not with servers. A noisy retry loop will blow the budget before the database does.

supporting.justification: Uploads have to live somewhere durable. The bucket is private. The app issues short-lived URLs. KYC, health, or customer files do not sit on a public CDN.

alternatives.why_not: A second file system splits retention and access reviews. One bucket next to the app is enough.

tradeoffs: Lifecycle rules are part of the design. Nobody deletes old uploads unless you ask the bucket to.

supporting.justification: realtime is true and the peak is 800. One Socket.IO process on the API covers chat and job status. Add the Valkey adapter only when you run a second copy.

alternatives.choice: A managed socket vendor (Ably or Pusher)
alternatives.why_not: A managed realtime vendor stores the hot path outside the region pin, and it is a new bill for a problem the API can hold.

tradeoffs: Sticky sessions or a pub/sub adapter are mandatory once you run two copies. One copy is a single point of failure.

supporting.justification: Payments in India, including UPI, should go through an RBI-authorised payment aggregator. Razorpay is that aggregator. Card numbers and UPI secrets stay on their side, which keeps this app out of full PCI scope.

alternatives.why_not: Cashfree is the other large India aggregator. Razorpay was chosen for payouts and the docs a small team will actually read.

tradeoffs: Do not store PAN, CVV, or UPI PIN. If you do, PCI scope explodes and this recommendation no longer holds.

supporting.justification: A short pipeline: test, then deploy with short-lived cloud credentials. Keep production secrets out of the repo.

alternatives.why_not: It is a fine CI. It is also a second account this team has not said they already run.

tradeoffs: A green pipeline is not a test plan. Someone still has to write the tests.

supporting.justification: Availability target is 99.9. You need a health check, a latency chart, and an alert that reaches a person. Keep the logs in the same region as the data.

alternatives.why_not: More moving parts, or a log vendor that may store text outside the pin.

tradeoffs: Log volume is a bill. Sample debug lines. Do not log OTP codes, tokens, or payment payloads.

assumptions: Compute (do_app, small band) about 12 to 50 USD.
PostgreSQL (do, small band) about 15 to 31 USD.
DigitalOcean Spaces is about 5 USD per month and includes 250 GiB.
Payment gateway fees are a percentage of volume and are not in this infra band.
SMS OTP is usage priced. The band assumes a fraction of users request a code each month, about 0.004 USD per active user, and ignores promotional SMS.
CI minutes are assumed inside the free tier for this team size.
Scale band is small: 30000 users at 12 months, peak 800, 50.0 GB stored.
This is an order-of-magnitude band, not an invoice. Taxes, support plans, and human time are excluded.

warnings.message: OTP SMS is usage priced and can pass the infra budget on its own. Cap retries, and watch the SMS bill as a separate line.
The MVP window is 8 weeks. A modular monolith across web, android usually wants about 10 weeks for a team this size. Cut scope before you cut the hard constraints.
DPDP applies. You still need a lawful purpose, a consent or legitimate-use record, a retention period, and a way for a person to access or erase their data. The region pin is not the whole duty.
Microservices and Kubernetes were not chosen. The team is 3 and the 12 month user count is 30,000. A single deployable is the design until those numbers move.
Keep card data at the payment aggregator and this app stays on the short PCI questionnaire. The moment you store PAN or CVV, stop and redesign.

assumptions: budget.existing_licences defaulted to an empty list.
scale.geographic_spread defaulted to national because data_residency is india.
data.sensitivity defaulted to confidential because a privacy law is set.
requirements.expected_rps_peak was not set. Capacity uses peak concurrency (800), which is roughly 80 requests per second if about one in ten connected users acts at once.
